claims.text: The intrinsic chemical composition of equimolar WTaTiVZr promotes nanoscale dispersoid formation during high-temperature deformation.
The nanoscale dispersoids interact with dislocations in WTaTiVZr.
Dislocation-dispersoid interactions facilitate continuous dynamic recovery.
Enhanced dynamic recovery produces a more stable dislocation network.
The stabilized dislocation network increases plastic strain relative to commercially pure tungsten.
The stabilized dislocation network increases toughness relative to commercially pure tungsten.
Identical powder-metallurgy and thermomechanical processing will ensure similar grain sizes in WTaTiVZr and pure tungsten.
Identical powder-metallurgy and thermomechanical processing will ensure similar initial dislocation densities in WTaTiVZr and pure tungsten.
Matching processing, grain size, and initial dislocation density isolates intrinsic chemical effects.
A controlled inert atmosphere minimizes oxidation during high-temperature deformation.
Dispersoid-assisted dynamic recovery promotes dislocation rearrangement and annihilation.
The resulting stabilized microstructure delays strain localization.
WTaTiVZr will develop a more equilibrated dislocation network than commercially pure tungsten during deformation.
WTaTiVZr will exhibit fewer localized stress concentrations than commercially pure tungsten.
Post-mortem high-resolution TEM will reveal nanoscale dispersoids in deformed WTaTiVZr.
WTaTiVZr will have a higher critical strain than identically processed commercially pure tungsten.
WTaTiVZr will have greater toughness than identically processed commercially pure tungsten.
Commercially pure tungsten will exhibit less dynamic recovery than WTaTiVZr under the specified conditions.
Commercially pure tungsten will develop a more disordered dislocation network without beneficial dispersoid interactions.
The proposed mechanism is limited to deformation at 1000–1400 °C in an inert atmosphere with controlled grain size.
